page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores running at 2.5 GHz, utilizing hyper-threading with 2 threads per core. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include any local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.se1.2xlarge exhibits modest processing capabilities. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench place the instance in the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show poor performance, falling into the bottom 10%. However, the instance demonstrates average capabilities in uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidth, as well as Passmark CPU physics and extended instruction tests. Redis SET operations and small-model (135M) LLM inference speeds also score in the middle 50% tier, whereas medium-model (7B) LLM inference is poor.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1.2xlarge offers a high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-frequency CPU performance. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs reduces overhead for deployments focused purely on memory capacity. This hardware profile is best suited for caching layers, in-memory databases like Redis, lightweight database operations, and general-purpose workloads requiring a larger memory footprint without intensive computational demands.
